big_case.notes: Private Maryland consumer-fraud and statutory attorney-fee dispute. The due-process hook (a recalled senior judge allegedly ineligible to sit while practicing law) is novel in framing but rests on a contested factual predicate the Appellate Court of Maryland found unproven, reaches the Court through an unreported intermediate opinion and a procedural dismissal by the Supreme Court of Maryland, alleges no split, and QP2 is pure state law. Respondents waived, one distribution, silent denial, no amici. Stakes confined to the parties.
